memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of iron‑deficiency anaemia, epilepsy and osteoporosis.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports no new seizures, mild fatigue over past month, denies bone pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 78 kg, height 1.70 m, BMI 27.0 (obese). Cardiovascular and respiratory systems normal. No focal neurological deficits. Spine tender minimally.
IMPRESSION: Iron‑deficiency anaemia persisting (Hb 9.2 g/dL, ferritin 12 ng/mL). Epilepsy well‑controlled on current regimen. Osteoporosis, BMI obese.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD, continue levetiracetam 500 mg BD and lamotrigine 50 mg BD, alendronate 70 mg once weekly, calcium 500 mg BD with vitamin D3 800 IU daily. Order fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar. Advise reduced‑calorie diet, brisk walk 30 min most days. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, blood in stools, worsening fatigue, new seizure activity, or sudden bone pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of anaemia response and medication tolerance.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Fatigue improved, occasional mild stomach upset with iron tablets, no seizures.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 77.5 kg, BMI 26.8 (overweight). Abdomen soft, no tenderness. Neurologic exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Haemoglobin risen to 10.8 g/dL, ferritin 28 ng/mL – partial response. Continue iron but reduce frequency to limit GI upset. Epilepsy stable. Osteoporosis unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Change ferrous sulfate to 200 mg on alternate days. Keep other meds. Reinforce diet‑iron rich foods, take tablets with food. Return if: worsening fatigue, black tarry stools, new seizure, severe abdominal pain, or BP >160/100.

memories.text: EEG performed – 20‑minute awake recording. Background activity normal for age. No epileptiform discharges, no spikes or sharp waves. No focal slowing. Interpretation: within normal limits, consistent with well‑controlled epilepsy on current regimen.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling a bit light‑headed when I stand up quickly, especially after morning walks. Wondering if the iron tablets or blood pressure meds could be causing this. No seizures, no chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: osteoporosis review and vitamin D status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No new bone pain, occasional light‑headedness on standing, denies seizures.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/78 mmHg, weight 77 kg, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Spine non‑tender, hips full range.
IMPRESSION: Orthostatic symptoms suggestive of mild volume depletion; vitamin D low (18 ng/mL). Osteoporosis: prior DEXA T‑score –2.6 at lumbar spine. Anaemia stable (Hb 10.8 g/dL). Epilepsy unchanged.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase vitamin D3 to 2000 IU daily, keep calcium 500 mg BD. Advise slow position changes, adequate hydration, salt intake if needed. Order repeat DEXA in 6 months and repeat vitamin D in 3 months. Return if: fainting, chest pain, new bone fracture, worsening dizziness, seizure, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up after DEXA and vitamin D repletion.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No light‑headedness, no seizures, feels well.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/76 mmHg, weight 76.5 kg, BMI 26.5 (overweight). No spinal tenderness.
IMPRESSION: DEXA lumbar spine T‑score –2.4 (improved from –2.6). Vitamin D now 32 ng/mL. Haemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, ferritin 35 ng/mL – mild iron deficiency but improving. Epilepsy seizure‑free.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue ferrous sulfate on alternate days, levetiracetam 500 mg BD, lamotrigine 50 mg BD, alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium 500 mg BD, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Advise maintain weight‑bearing exercise, calcium‑rich diet. Return if: new bone pain, fracture, seizure activity, chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39°C, or worsening anaemia symptoms.
